label: def:ast
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:ast}
The relations $R_i$ are the orbits of $G$ on $X\times X$ (the \emph{orbital
relations}):  $R_i$ is the set of \emph{ordered} pairs $(X,Y)\in X^2$ whose
relative position is fixed by the stabilizer, i.e.\ $(X,Y)$ and $(X',Y')$
lie in the same $R_i$ iff some $g\in G$ sends $(X,Y)$ to $(X',Y')$.  The
diagonal pairs $(X,X)$ form one relation per fiber $X_i^G$
($i=1,\ldots,\sigma_3$), which coincide into a single diagonal relation
$R_0$ when $G$ is transitive on $X$ (i.e.\ $\sigma_3=1$).  The data
$(X,\{R_0,\ldots,R_s\})$ define the \emph{Schurian coherent configuration}
$\mathfrak{X}(G)$ of $G$ on triples;  when every orbital relation is
homogeneous, this is an association scheme (the \emph{Schurian association
scheme}) on triples.
head: environment
name: Schurian coherent configuration on triples

label: prop:valencies
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:valencies}
Let $X=\binom{\mathcal{P}}{3}$, and let $X_1^G,\dots,X_{\sigma_3}^G$ be the
$G$-orbits on $X$, with representatives $X_i$ and stabilizers
$H_i=G_{X_i}$ ($\sigma_3$ as in \textup{Remark \ref{rem:char}}).
For each $i,j$, write
\[
\rho_{ij}=\#\bigl\{\text{$H_i$-orbits on }X_j^G\bigr\}\qquad(H_i=G_{X_i});
\]
$\rho_{ii}$ counts, in particular, the fixed point $X_i$ itself (the diagonal
pair $(X_i,X_i)$), so $\rho_{ii}\ge1$.  The relations of $\mathfrak{X}(G)$ are
the orbits of $G$ on $X\times X$;  each relation is determined uniquely by the
pair $(i,j)$ of its first- and second-coordinate fibers and by an $H_i$-orbit
on $X_j^G$ (fixing the representative $X_i$), so the class number is
\[
m=\#\{\text{orbital relations of }\mathfrak{X}(G)\}
=\sum_{i=1}^{\sigma_3}\sum_{j=1}^{\sigma_3}\rho_{ij}.
\]
The number of orbital relations is called the \emph{rank} of $G$ on $X$ only
in the transitive case $\sigma_3=1$;  for $\sigma_3>1$ the term \emph{rank}
is not used.
The diagonal contributes one relation per fiber (the trivial $H_i$-orbit
$X_i$), i.e.\ $\sigma_3$ diagonal relations in total.  The valencies of the
relations issued from the fiber $X_i^G$ are the sizes of the $H_i$-suborbits
on the target fibers $X_j^G$, whose sums are $|X_j^G|=|G|/|H_j|$, the orbit
sizes of \textup{Table \ref{tab:main}}.  The scheme is symmetric (every
relation is self-paired) if and only if $G$ is generously transitive on
triples; for $Sym(\mathcal{P})$ the relations are the overlap classes
$\{|X\cap Y|=0,1,2,3\}$ and the scheme is symmetric.
head: environment
name: Class number and valencies

title: Proof
body_md:
The relations of a Schurian coherent configuration are the orbits of $G$ on $X\times X$, so
their number is the number of orbital relations (the rank of $G$ on $X$
when $\sigma_3=1$).  Fix the representatives $X_i$, one
per fiber.  Each relation $R$ has a unique first-coordinate fiber $X_i^G$
and a unique second-coordinate fiber $X_j^G$; the relations with these two
fibers are in bijection with the $H_i$-orbits on $X_j^G$ via
$R\longmapsto\{Y\in X_j^G:(X_i,Y)\in R\}$ (each pair $(X_i,Y)$ determines one
relation; distinct $H_i$-orbits give distinct $G$-orbits, and every $G$-orbit
arises from its unique first-coordinate fiber), whence
$m=\sum_{i=1}^{\sigma_3}\sum_{j=1}^{\sigma_3}\rho_{ij}$, as stated.  The
diagonal pairs $(X_i,X_i)$ form one orbit per fiber (the trivial $H_i$-orbit),
so the diagonal contributes $\sigma_3$ relations.  The valency of the
relation through $Y\in X_j^G$ is $|Y^{H_i}|$, and the $H_i$-suborbits
partition $X_j^G$, whose size is $|G|/|H_j|$ by the orbit--stabilizer
theorem.  Symmetry means that $(X,Y)$ and $(Y,X)$ lie in the same relation
for every pair, i.e.\ that $G_{X,Y}$ contains an element interchanging $X$
and $Y$; this is the classical notion of generous transitivity on triples
(see \cite[Chapter~1]{muller2009}).  For $Sym(\mathcal{P})$ the $G_{X,Y}$-stabilizer
obviously contains such an element (any bijection swapping the two triples),
and the relation of a pair is determined by the overlap $|X\cap Y|$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
The intersection numbers $p_{ij}^k$ of $\mathfrak{X}(G)$ are determined by the
suborbits of the two-point stabilizers: writing $X=\{a,b,c\}$ and letting
$Y=\{a',b',c'\}$ run over the triples with fixed relative position to $X$,
the count depends on the $G_{\{a,b\}}$-suborbit data of
\textup{Proposition \ref{prop:pair-orbits}}.  The general closed formula is due to Mesner and
Bhattacharya \cite{mesner1990}; the specific numerical ASTs of the
$2$-transitive families are tabulated in \cite{balmaceda2021}.  In the
Steiner case $\lambda=1$, the block graph
$\overline{\Gamma}(\mathcal{T})$ of \textup{Theorem \ref{thm:stblock}(ii)} is a strongly
regular graph.  On the block fiber the graph relations induce a two-class
\emph{fusion} of the coherent configuration induced by $\mathfrak{X}(G)$ on
that fiber:  the adjacency relation ``meeting in exactly one point'' is in
general a union of $G$-orbital relations, and the graph is identified with an
orbital scheme only when that relation is a single orbital;  for the affine
STS$(q)$ under $AGL(1,q)$, $q\equiv0\pmod3$, this recovers the
classical affine schemes.
head: environment
name: Intersection numbers

label: prop:ast-closed
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:ast-closed}
Let $\mathcal{T}_i$ be a single orbit triple system (block-transitive, with
representative $X_i$ and stabilizer $H_i=G_{X_i}$), and let
$\mathfrak{X}(G)$ be the Schurian coherent configuration of
\textup{Proposition \ref{prop:valencies}}.  The full intersection table
$\{p_{jk}^\ell\}$ of $\mathfrak{X}(G)$ can in principle be computed from the
following data --- a computational scheme rather than a closed
determination:  the two-point data below are essential inputs to the
Mesner--Bhattacharya formula \cite{mesner1990}, and no claim is made that
the data determine the table without it:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the $H_i$-suborbit (valency) arrays of \textup{Proposition \ref{prop:valencies}}, computed by the suborbit method (the stabilizer orders $|H_i|$ alone do not determine the orbit decomposition:  the $H_i$-action on the target fiber must be known, or the double cosets computed);
\item the two-point stabilizer suborbit data of \textup{Proposition \ref{prop:pair-orbits}}, which control the relative position of a pair $(Y,Z)$ of blocks above a fixed block $X_i$ (these are essential:  an intersection number counts blocks $Z$ with fixed position relative to an \emph{ordered} block pair, a two-point datum not recoverable from two-point orbit lengths alone);
\item in the Steiner case $\lambda=1$, the strongly regular block graph of \textup{Theorem \ref{thm:stblock}(ii)} \textup{(its $\lambda,\mu$ parameters are the relevant $p_{jk}^\ell$ above the one-point layer)}.
\end{enumerate}
The valency arrays of (1) alone do not determine the full table:  the two-point
  stabilizer suborbit data of (2) are essential, since $p_{jk}^\ell$ counts blocks whose
  position relative to an ordered block pair is fixed, a two-point datum.  The general
  closed formula realizing this reduction is Mesner--Bhattacharya's
\cite{mesner1990};  the numerical tables of the $2$-transitive families are in
\cite{balmaceda2021}, and the values of \textup{Proposition \ref{prop:astnum}}
($m=32$ for $AGL(1,7)$, $m=1814$ for $PSU(3,3)$, with the displayed
double-index arrays) are computed from the explicit actions and checked
against the orbit sizes.
For the Suzuki and Ree rows the ingredients are explicit:  the orbit
sizes are $|G|/|H_i|$ with the stabilizer orders of
\textup{Theorems \ref{thm:sz-orbits} and \ref{thm:ree-structure}}, and the
valency arrays can then be obtained by the suborbit method of (1);  the
full intersection tables of these rows would then follow from the
Mesner--Bhattacharya formula, whose two-point inputs remain to be computed
case by case.
head: environment
name: Computational reduction of the intersection numbers

title: Proof
body_md:
The relations of $\mathfrak{X}(G)$ are the $G$-orbits on $X_i^G\times X_i^G$,
indexed by the $H_i$-suborbits (1).  An intersection number
$p_{jk}^\ell$ counts, for a fixed ordered pair $(X_i,Y)$ in the $j$-th
relation, the number of $Z$ in the $k$-th relation with $(X_i,Z)$ in the
$\ell$-th relation;  this is a count over triples $Z$ whose relative position
to both $X_i$ and $Y$ is fixed, and the position relative to the pair
$\{X_i,Y\}$ is governed by the two-point stabilizer suborbits (2), exactly
as in \textup{Proposition \ref{prop:pair-orbits}}.  The Steiner case reduces to
the block graph because for $\lambda=1$ the position of $Z$ relative to a
pair of blocks meeting in one point is decided by the $9$ or $(v-5)/2+4$
common neighbors of \textup{Theorem \ref{thm:stblock}(ii)}, giving (3).  The
remaining assertions record where the ingredients occur in this monograph.

label: prop:astnum
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:astnum}
For the affine row $AGL(1,7)$ on the $35$ triples:  $\sigma_3=2$ and the
two orbits contribute the full double-index array
$\rho_{11}=6$, $\rho_{12}=7$, $\rho_{21}=7$, $\rho_{22}=12$;  the diagonal
suborbit (valency) arrays are $1^2\,3^{4}$ (on the $14$-block orbit,
$|G_X|=3$) and $1^3\,2^{9}$ (on the $21$-block orbit, $|G_X|=2$), and the
cross-fiber arrays are $3^{7}$ resp.\ $2^{7}$, so the class number is
\[
m=\rho_{11}+\rho_{12}+\rho_{21}+\rho_{22}=6+7+7+12=32;
\]
For $PSU(3,3)$ on the $3276$ triples:  $\sigma_3=3$ and the full
double-index array is
\[
(\rho_{ij})=\begin{pmatrix}13&44&84\\44&193&338\\84&338&676\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
m=\sum_{i,j}\rho_{ij}=13+44+84+44+193+338+84+338+676=1814;
\]
the diagonal suborbit arrays are $1\,3\,8\,24^{10}$ (collinear orbit, $252$
blocks, $|G_X|=24$), $1^3\,3^{45}\,6^{145}$ ($1008$ blocks, $|G_X|=6$) and
$1^6\,3^{670}$ ($2016$ blocks, $|G_X|=3$), and the cross-fiber arrays are
$12^4\,24^{40}$ and $24^{84}$ (from the collinear stabilizer on the $1008$-
and $2016$-block fibers), $3^4\,6^{40}$ and $2^3\,6^{335}$ (from the
$1008$-block stabilizer), and $3^{84}$ and $1^3\,3^{335}$ (from the
$2016$-block stabilizer).  These numbers are computed with the explicit
$3$-dimensional unitary representation of $PSU(3,3)$ over
$\mathbb{F}_9$ (the $28$ absolutely singular projective points;  the group
order $6048$ is verified), and each array sums to the corresponding orbit
size, which is a cross-check of the computation.
